summary: The recovery drill on a small GRUB disk with the three partitions of an installed machine: a root destroyed and rewritten through recovery over SSH, the fallback past a recovery payload that does not load, and recovery reached through the core image and on a network with no DHCP server; the program is tests/cases/machine/drill_scenario.c

cases.behavior: one copy of the drill disk booted through SeaBIOS and GRUB again and again: the everyday kernel refuses to write its own disk and writes nothing; a destroyed root stops the boot without a login; the armed recovery entry comes up from partition 2, takes a lease and answers SSH with nothing typed at its console; the whole root arrives through one ssh pipe; recovery saved as the default comes back after a power cut; the machine boots from the repaired root; a recovery payload that will not load falls back to partition 1; and a destroyed partition 1 still reaches recovery through the core image

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the copy of the disk; the scenario removes the copy of the demo key, the root image it sent and the saved copy of the disk; both keep theirs after a failure

steps.does: boot the declared Rach2 OpenSSH client and open its framed command channel
boot the disk through SeaBIOS and GRUB, log in as root at the console, try reflash and a shell redirect into /dev/disk0, halt, and compare the copy's first sector with the disk's
zero the root's superblock in the copy, boot it until the kernel halts for want of a root, and end it with QMP's quit

arm the recovery entry in the copy's environment block, boot it with a card, wait for init's record of starting the SSH server, try ssh until it answers, and read the service log, /dev/disk0 and the raw writers' rules over SSH
restart the Rach2 client with the extracted root as its declared raw input disk
send the root as built from the client's attached raw disk through one SSH connection to reflash, sync, and compare the copy's root partition with it
read the saved default with bootctl, save recovery as the default, and power the machine off over SSH
boot the copy with nothing armed, reach recovery over SSH, put the saved default back, and power it off
boot the copy until it asks for a login, and end it with QMP's quit
save the copy, zero the first MiB of partition 2, arm recovery, boot until a login, end it with QMP's quit, and put the copy back
zero the first 2 MiB of partition 1, boot until recovery's shell, run a command there, and end it with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the disk's MBR has partitions 1 and 2 and one entry of type 0x83, the root, and the disk has GRUB's environment block
reflash of /dev/disk0 by the everyday kernel, whose ext2 root is mounted, says Resource busy
the shell's redirect into /dev/disk0 says cannot open a redirection, before halt powers the machine off
the copy's first sector is the disk's after the refused writes
with the root's superblock destroyed, the kernel says the root has no ext2 file system this kernel mounts, and halts
that boot asks for no login
the armed recovery entry boots the recovery image, whose init says so
after init says it started the SSH server, a command runs as root by the demo key, tried again only while ssh fails
recovery's service log has udhcpc's lease
recovery has /dev/disk0 as a block device
reflash refuses a write that runs past the end of the device
/dev/grubcore opens for writing on its own
/dev/grubcore does not open for writing while /dev/disk0 is held open for writing
reflash reports the root partition's whole length written from the ssh pipe
after a sync, the copy's root partition has the bytes of the image sent
bootctl reads the saved default back as candidate or fallback
bootctl saves recovery as the default and reads it back
after the power cut, with nothing armed, the saved default boots the recovery image
that recovery answers a key login after init starts its server, tried again only while ssh fails
the machine that came back has /dev/disk0, as recovery has
bootctl puts back the saved default read before the repair, and reads it back
the ordinary entry boots the repaired machine to a login prompt
the kernel says ext2: root: on that boot
with partition 2 destroyed and recovery armed, the machine still reaches a login prompt
that boot mounts the ext2 root
that boot loads no RAM image, so it was a kernel on partition 1 and not recovery
with partition 1 destroyed, the machine reaches recovery's shell, which runs a command
that boot says modules: found 1, the recovery image

native.reason: the drill destroys and rewrites the disk the machine boots from, between boots and from the host, and reads the result off a copy the host compares

cases.behavior: the recovery artifact check refuses the everyday kernel, and the recovery kernel, booted from a RAM image, publishes /dev/disk0 with no rach2.diskdiag on its command line

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the copy of the disk, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: run the tree's tools/inspect/check_recovery.sh on the everyday kernel, asking for the recovery authority
boot the recovery kernel and image directly with rach2.root=ram and the disk on IDE, test for /dev/disk0 at recovery's shell, and end it with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: check_recovery.sh exits 1 on the everyday kernel asked for the recovery authority, and says the kernel does not carry the recovery banner
the recovery kernel has /dev/disk0 as a block device, with no rach2.diskdiag on its command line

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case reads a built kernel off the host and boots the recovery kernel, which a running machine cannot become

cases.behavior: the recovery kernel and image, booted directly as the core image boots them, on a card on a hub of QEMU's with nothing else on it, where no DHCP server answers, take the fixed address 192.168.0.105 and stop the DHCP client

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the copy of the disk, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the recovery kernel and image directly with rach2.slot=recovery and rach2.ip=none, its card on a hub of its own, and wait for recovery's shell

wait for the kernel's record of eth0's first address, then at recovery's shell for rescue-static's line in the service log, read eth0's address and look for udhcpc, and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the first address the kernel records for eth0 is 192.168.0.105/24, the fixed one, and no lease came before it
once rescue-static logs the fixed address, ifconfig gives eth0 that address
then no udhcpc runs, so no later lease can replace the address

native.reason: the case needs a machine whose network has no DHCP server, which the case makes by putting the emulated card on a hub of QEMU's with nothing else on it
